source.title: Dual-Space Smoothness for Robust and Balanced LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Hang Yan; Zhe-Yuan Liu; Meng Jiang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fine-tuning on forget-set subsets and jailbreak prompts recover behavior after unlearning, and reports PRISM as a counter-method. It argues that existing methods have robustness limitations and that PRISM improves resistance, with incomplete resistance in some settings.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported MUSE-Books relearning KnowMem results, WMDPbio jailbreak ASRs, and the RMU-family relearning KnowMem results in Table 4. The paper also reports related Table 2 VerbMem and utility values, MUSE-News relearning, 100- and 200-example relearning, and additional jailbreak results on Ministral; these are omitted under the 60-row cap. Prior-work results are not recorded. Representation-margin results are not rows for version C: they do not test whether an internal edit restores knowledge or show that knowledge is blocked rather than deleted. No quantization experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study runs forget-subset relearning attacks (MUSE-Books/News) and jailbreaks (WMDPbio) on existing unlearned models. It reports how much forgotten knowledge or harmful output returns, and tests its own counter-method, PRISM, against the same attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also say low ASR and low recall for GA and NPO reflect catastrophic collapse, not robust forgetting. Their robustness claim for PRISM rests mainly on VerbMem, utility and Unlearn Score. Its 100-step KnowMem recovery (33.045) is about the same as the baselines', which they attribute to GA/GAGDR collapse when comparing.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces PRISM, combining a robust representation probe, parameter-space smoothness and gradient-conflict decoupling; evaluates existing methods and attacks rather than reproducing an original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning step count and sample size, dataset and model; jailbreak method and prefill length; for PRISM, smoothness radius, probe adversarial weight and probe layer also change results.

fits_no_version.finding: Relearning on a small forget subset collapses SAM+NPO's retain utility (32.8 to 8.7 at 50 steps; Fig. 5, Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relearning attacks can destroy general utility in sharpness-regularized unlearned models rather than restoring knowledge.

record.code_released: Code is stated to be available in Supplementary Materials; no URL stated.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the attack or recovery values. The Table 2 MUSE-Books relearning subset size is not stated. Low ASR and low memory measures for some methods are attributed by the authors to catastrophic utility collapse, complicating interpretation as robust forgetting. The evidence is limited to the reported benchmarks, methods and attack budgets.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row cap, omitted Table 2 VerbMem and utility metrics; Table 4 PRISM and other methods beyond the two RMU-family KnowMem rows; MUSE-News relearning (Table 10); 100- and 200-example relearning (Tables 4 and 18); the Table 5 ablation; and Ministral jailbreak results (Table 11). Selected rows prioritize direct forget-set recovery metrics and per-attack WMDPbio ASRs. Representation-margin results (Table 17) do not test recovery or distinguish deletion from blocked access.

untested.parts: Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; only random forget-set subsets are used.
Entire version: no direction ablation and no blocked-vs-deleted analysis. The Table 17 probe margins measure PRISM's mechanism, not recovery.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information; recovery of WMDP multiple-choice accuracy under prompting.
Resistance to quantization, direction ablation and unrelated-data relearning.

missing.what: WMDP and WMDPbio accuracy with MMLU and HellaSwag for all methods on Llama-2-7B and Ministral-8B; near-chance WMDPbio comes with near-chance MMLU on Llama-2.
Table 2 KnowMem for NPOGDR at 75 and 100 steps (14.305, 33.750) and GA at 50 steps (0.915); the rows mis-assign values and name no methods.
NPO on MUSE-News: the unlearning effect reverts after more than 100 relearning steps.

record.verdict_notes: Row versions V1–V6 are mapped to A–F. Jailbreak ASR is an LLM-judge harmfulness rate on mixed SORRY-Bench/HEx-PHI/WMDPbio prompts. The forget set includes general harmful requests, so the WMDP 'unlearning' is partly refusal training. No unattacked ASR for unlearned models is given, so E evidence is indirect. The relearning subset size for Table 2 is not stated. The study proposes PRISM and is not an original source for F.

versions.untested_parts: No explicit chance-level reference is given, and the results do not establish that all methods retain general ability while reaching near chance. The study tests selected methods and attacks on its chosen benchmarks.
Tests fine-tuning on subsets of the original forget set, not unrelated or loosely related examples. The Table 2 attack sample size is not stated.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test distinguishing access-blocking from deletion.
Tests prefill, AutoDAN and multi-turn jailbreak attacks on WMDPbio; does not test rephrasing alone, other languages or in-context information as separate conditions.
Tests PRISM against the reported relearning and jailbreak attacks; does not establish resistance to every attack type in the claim.
